body.statement:
Let \(k=|T|\), \(w_q=2^{1-K_f}c_q\), and \(L=\eta+(1-\eta)/\alpha\).  For every \((\mathbf X_n,P_{\beta,n})\in\mathfrak M\), every \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), every balanced \(T\) with \(k\geq Q\), and every \(H\in\mathcal H_T\),
\[
 V_T(H,\beta)
 \leq \frac{4LQ}{3\eta^2k^2}
 \left\{\max_{q\in\mathcal Q}w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\right\}
 \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}E_\beta\{Y_{in}(q)^2\mid x_{in}\}.
\]
Consequently, the asserted uniform \(O(k^{-1})\) conclusion holds on every subclass for which the displayed average second-moment envelope is bounded uniformly over its members, parameters, and balanced subsets.  No supremum over all of \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted without such a common numerical envelope.
body.justification: Positive assignment support makes every permitted one-wave Horvitz--Thompson risk uniformly first order even on irregular subsets.
body.gap: General Horvitz--Thompson consistency does not provide a constant uniform over the present pilot-indexed rerandomization actions.
body.consumer: It rules out apparent gains from assigning only a vanishing main wave and controls rare singular pilot complements.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the potential-outcome table and let \(U_T\) denote the uniform law on \(\Omega_T\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}mixture}\),
\[
 \frac{p_{T,H}(z)}{U_T(z)}
 =\eta+\frac{1-\eta}{\alpha}a_{T,H}(z)\leq L,
 \qquad
 \pi_{iq}(T,H)\geq\frac{\eta}{Q}.
 \tag{3}
\]
For a scalar coordinate after applying \(W^{1/2}\), write the estimator as
\[
 k^{-1}\sum_{i\in T}f_i(Z_i),
 \qquad
 f_i(q)=\frac{e^{\mathsf T}W^{1/2}w_qY_{in}(q)}{\pi_{iq}(T,H)},
\]
where \(e\) is a Euclidean coordinate vector.  Under balanced complete randomization, direct enumeration of the two labels assigned to distinct units gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{U_T}\{f_i(Z_i),f_j(Z_j)\}
 =-\frac{1}{k-1}\operatorname{Cov}_{q\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal Q)}\{f_i(q),f_j(q)\},
 \qquad i\ne j.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{U_T}\!\left\{\sum_{i\in T}f_i(Z_i)\right\}
 &=\frac{k}{k-1}\sum_{i\in T}\operatorname{Var}_{q}\{f_i(q)\}
 -\frac{1}{k-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q}\!\left\{\sum_{i\in T}f_i(q)\right\}\\
 &\leq \frac{k}{k-1}\sum_{i\in T}E_q f_i(q)^2.
 \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(c=E_{U_T}[k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)]\).  Exact Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness under \(p_{T,H}\), proved in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}ht\text{-}accounting}\), and the likelihood-ratio bound (3) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_{T,H}}\!\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)\right\}
 \leq E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)-c\right\}^2\right]
 \leq L\operatorname{Var}_{U_T}\!\left\{k^{-1}\sum_i f_i(Z_i)\right\}.
\]
Sum this inequality over an orthonormal coordinate basis and use (3)--(4).  Since \(k\geq Q=2^{K_f}\geq4\), one has \(k/(k-1)\leq4/3\).  Therefore, conditional on the table,
\[
 E_{p_{T,H}}\!\left[
 (\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)^{\mathsf T}
 W(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}^{\mathrm{HT}}_T(H)-\boldsymbol\tau_T)
 \right]
 \leq \frac{4LQ}{3\eta^2k^2}
 \left\{\max_q w_q^{\mathsf T}Ww_q\right\}
 \sum_{i\in T}\sum_qY_{in}(q)^2.
\]
Averaging over \(P_{\beta,n}(d\mathbf Y_n\mid\mathbf X_n)\) proves the displayed claim.  In particular a common bound on the average conditional second moment makes the right-hand side a common constant times \(k^{-1}\).

The original supremum over all members of \(\mathfrak M\) cannot be recovered from \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\): that assumption supplies only a memberwise finite bound and fixes no common numerical envelope.  More concretely, start from any admissible bounded regular conditional family and apply the one-to-one rescaling \(Y(q)\mapsto M Y(q)\).  For each finite \(M\) the memberwise boundedness, quadratic-mean differentiability, and Fisher information are preserved under this pushforward; the trace-normalized oracle action is unchanged, while every quadratic design risk is multiplied by \(M^2\).  Letting \(M\) range over finite constants is an explicit generic-class certificate that the unqualified model-class supremum is infinite.
